halak with the particle of the English phrasal verb the ASV renders it by, headed on the verb (rule 44). This is not rule 44's surplus particle: *away* states the separation the clause already writes in me'et, so it adds no direction, result or repetition the Hebrew lacks, which is the second condition that test requires and the one the *back* of bo' hiphil -> *bring him back* meets. The bare verb writing the lexeme cannot be the whole test, since matsa' -> *find out*, kanas -> *gather together* and natan -> *put away* keep their particles on that same footing. The preposition's own English word is *from*, and the particle is the verb's rendering rather than a second word offered to that preposition. Competing reading: mark *away* `added`, which is how this verse was first aligned; JDG.19.28 keeps the *up* of *took her up upon the ass* on the reading taken here.
